messages:
alex: quick thread: proposing a clear resume/abort policy for shard uploads + hot-cache fallback heuristics. want buy-in before I add to ingest RFC.

dina: do it. current behavior is a bit ad-hoc when uploads fail mid-shard.

alex: goals: 1) deterministic final state (committed/aborted/stale), 2) cheap resume (client can resume from last acknowledged chunk), 3) safe runtime fallback if commit delayed, 4) observable reasons for aborts.

michael: how do you distinguish "stale" vs "aborted"?

alex: definitions: "staging" = in-progress ingest; "committed" = atomic commit marker present; "aborted" = client signaled abort OR checksum mismatch on finalization; "stale" = staging not touched for >t_dead (configurable) and automatically tombstoned.

dina: what is t_dead? 1 hour? depends on average upload speed and shard sizes. we should compute it per-checkpoint: t_dead = max(1h, expected_upload_time*3).

tara: expected_upload_time derived from shard size and ingest-policy for region and bandwidth quotas. good idea.

michael: resume flow sketch: client POST /v1/ingest-checkpoint/{id}/resume -> server returns per-shard next_offset + list of verified chunks. client streams remaining chunks with headers X-Chunk-Offset and X-Chunk-Checksum. server appends and updates running_digest. final POST /commit triggers conditional write.

alex: server must persist idempotency tokens for each chunk upload (client-provided upload_id) to avoid duplicate-appends on retry. store minimal chunk index metadata: offset, length, checksum.

dina: what about partial overlapping chunk uploads (client sends offset=0 again due to bad resume logic)? server should detect overlap and reject if checksum differs. allow reupload only for exact matching chunk metadata.

michael: agree. reject overlapping writes unless exact offset/length/checksum match an already-ack record.

tara: runtime fallback: if a checkpoint remains in staging for >t_serve (shorter than t_dead) runtime can choose to serve an older compatible checkpoint or route to derived artifact. we need a clear routing precedence: committed(indexed) > committed(unindexed) > compatible-derived > legacy > serve-failure.

alex: and include a 'staging_visibility' flag: by default staging is invisible to runtime, but if a user explicitly requests early access (for fast internal iteration) the ingest client can set "expose_staging_for_internal": true which sets a time-limited preview token. runtime must refuse preview tokens from public routes.

dina: preview tokens should be scoped and audited. add a short TTL (10m) and require developer role to create. log all preview access.

michael: backpressure: runtime can set a per-node soft quota for concurrent staging-checkpoints being pulled. ingest should respect a backoff header in manifest fetch responses: Retry-After or X-Warmup-Backoff suggesting ms to wait before streaming.

tara: suggestion: manifest includes "warmup_priority" integer. scheduler picks highest priority while honoring per-node concurrency and total pending bytes. warmup_priority computed from route SLA and model popularity.

alex: eviction interplay: if a shard stream fails mid-warmup and node is low on memory, we should free partially-filled buffers but keep checkpoint staging metadata so client can resume later. partially-filled buffers must be zeroed and recorded in metrics: partial_warmup_evictions.

dina: and if a node crashes mid-warmup, on restart it should replay session state from catalog plus ephemeral session token to continue streaming if within TTL. otherwise client must re-resume. avoid long-lived sessions.

michael: CRCs: per-tensor + per-chunk checksums preferred. client reports per-chunk checksum; runtime validates per-tensor checksum during streaming. if mismatch after commit, mark checkpoint corrupted and automatically mark derived artifacts stale.

tara: how to handle "competing commits" from two ingest clients for same logical model version? commit should be conditional on a staging-version token: commit if metadata.version==expected. if conflict return 409 with latest state. clients must be prepared to fetch latest and reapply.

alex: migration: legacy checkpoints without staging metadata will be treated as committed-but-unverified. we should mark them with "verification_state": "unknown" and allow runtime to opt-in via a compatibility whitelist. schedule a background verifier to backfill verification and index generation.

dina: observability: emit events for every state transition: staging_created, chunk_ack, staging_heartbeat, commit_attempt, commit_success, commit_conflict, abort, tombstone. make audit URL available: /ingest/{id}/events.

michael: alarms: if a bucket sees >X tombstones per minute, raise SRE alert. tombstones likely indicate client-bug or exporter flakiness.

tara: security: preview tokens + resume tokens must be HMAC-signed with ingest service key and include bounds: allowed ip ranges, ttl, and allowed scopes (read-only vs write). runtime must verify HMAC before allowing resume.

alex: propose TTLs: resume token = 24h, preview token = 10m, session token (for streaming decrypt) = 1h. configurable per-deployment.

dina: costs: resuming and keeping staging rows has catalog storage cost. tombstone rows should be GC'd after t_dead_long (e.g., 30 days) but keep minimal audit record for compliance.

michael: scripts: add a small client library helper: IngestClient.resume(id) which handles token refresh, chunk parallelism (bounded), checksum reporting, and exponential backoff on 409. keep this in devex.

tara: plus runtime helper: WarmupManager.pull(checkpoint_id, budget_bytes) which honors warmup_priority, backoff headers, and exposes partial_progress metrics.

alex: final ask: thumbs up to add these semantics to the RFC and include the helper libs as part of initial prototype?

dina: +1

michael: +1, please add clear failure modes and client pseudocode in RFC.

tara: +1, especially want the observable events and tombstone alarms.

resume-bot: resume-policy proposal 4623456789 accepted by eng-ml reviewers: dina, michael, tara at 2026-03-12T09:07:16Z :white_check_mark:
